Signers

Who is on duty, and what they are signing. Everything here is read from the pool — nothing on this page can start, stop or authorise anything. A signer appears only if it is set to announce itself; one that stays quiet still shows up under its signatures below. New to this? How it works · in business terms.

On duty

Each row is one device. It signed its own announcement with a key it claims to hold, so the label and the keys are the device's own word, proven. Fresh means it spoke within the pool's freshness window; the age is always shown beside it, because "quiet" and "gone" are different facts.

In the pool

Transactions waiting for signatures, newest first, with the devices that have signed each one — matched by public key against the roster above. The pool keeps a transaction for about an hour from its start time, so this is a live window, not a record. Verdicts are what a signer decided, and a signer only reports on transactions addressed to it: its own deals, needing one of its keys. An empty verdicts cell means nobody who is watching had any business with this transaction — the ordinary case on a shared pool, not a missing answer.

Reads ?action=signers, ?action=txList and ?action=txRead from the pool pass-through next to this page. Point it somewhere else with ?api=https://host/future/. Every control is in the URL, so a link shows the same view to whoever opens it.

Tap a pooled transaction to inspect it — the same widget the signing page uses. Add ?readonly=1 for a link that can inspect but not sign, or ?open=pool (also duty, seen, all, none) to point a link at one section. Each section's raw ↗ link is the exact GET behind it.
